top_story: The war is reshaping the Middle East through civilian devastation as much as battlefield escalation, with millions of children facing death, displacement, trauma, forced migration, and recruitment into armed groups. That social collapse now intersects with a sharper US-Iran confrontation after an F-15E Strike Eagle was shot down over Iran, leaving one US crew member rescued and the other missing in the first loss of a US fighter jet in this war. Trump’s threat to destroy Iran’s power plants unless Tehran reopens the Strait of Hormuz has pushed the confrontation toward infrastructure warfare, drawing Iranian military and political warnings that any further strike could widen the conflict across the Gulf. The conflict is no longer only a contest over military deterrence; it is becoming a regional crisis in which attacks on strategic assets and the destruction of civilian life are reinforcing each other.
